doctrine: Agents propose. Humans judge. Nurses steward.
purpose: Judgment support is a runtime feature, not advice: answers arrive framed, probed, and carrying a visible reasoning ledger so the accountable human can actually judge them. The layer strengthens judgment; it never replaces it.
notice: Structured for your judgment: assumptions, alternatives, and change conditions are listed for you to weigh — this is a feature, not a disclaimer. Agents propose. Humans judge. Nurses steward.

clinical_judgment.label: Clinical judgment — notice, interpret, respond, reflect
probes: Before the answer: what did you notice first in this situation, and what does it make you expect next?
Which cue here matters most, and which cue might you be over-weighting?
What would you do first — and what observation would tell you it was the wrong first move?
Looking back on a similar situation, what did you learn that applies here?

systems.label: Systems lens — upstream, downstream, feedback
probes: Who is upstream of this problem, and who inherits whatever you change?
What loop keeps this problem alive — and what currently benefits from the loop?
If this fix works perfectly, what second-order effect appears in three months?
Which part of this is a person problem, and which part is the system producing exactly what it was designed to produce?

design.label: Design studio — audience, options, prototype
probes: Who will actually use this, and what have they said in their own words?
What are two genuinely different ways to do this — not variations of one idea?
What is the smallest version you could put in front of a real person this week?
What would make the intended audience quietly ignore this?

evidence.label: Evidence appraisal — claim, source, limitation
probes: What claim are you actually testing, and what would count as evidence against it?
Which of your sources is strongest, and what is its most important limitation?
Where do policy, research, and local practice disagree here?
Which assumption in this question has never been confirmed?

general.label: General judgment — assumptions, alternatives, change conditions
probes: What is your own read before you see mine?
What assumption would hurt most if it turned out wrong?
What alternative did you already rule out, and why?
What new information would change your mind?
